fields.billingAmountHelp: Keep it short, for example “50% prepayment, $900”. Put the reason, the base amount and the remainder in the billing notes.

inputs.progressNotes: Homepage redesign done, waiting for the client’s review by Friday. Next: inner pages, starting Monday. No blockers.

example.intro: Plain notes in any order are enough. For example:
example.output:
Hello,

Quick update on the redesign: the homepage is done and ready for your review by Friday. From Monday I move on to the inner pages. No blockers so far.

Please send your comments on the homepage by Friday so the inner pages can build on the approved version.

inputs.clientMessage: Hi, can you also add a blog section? And could we have everything a week earlier?
inputs.replyGoal: Agree to the blog as a paid add-on, keep the original deadline, offer a short call.

example.intro: Paste the client’s message and say what the reply should achieve. For example:
example.output:
Hi,

Happy to add a blog section. It is outside the agreed scope, so I will send you a short estimate for it today. Moving the whole delivery a week earlier is not realistic without cutting quality, so I suggest keeping the original date and delivering the homepage first.

Would a 15-minute call tomorrow work to agree on the details?

inputs.billingNotes: Agreed budget for the landing page design: $1,800. The 50% prepayment ($900) books the team’s time; the remaining $900 is due after the mockup is delivered. Payment details will come in a separate invoice.

example.intro: The amount stays short; the reason, the base and the remainder go to the notes. For example:
example.output:
Hello,

To book the team’s time for the landing page design, please make the 50% prepayment of $900 of the agreed $1,800 budget within 4 days. The remaining $900 is due after the mockup is delivered. The payment details will follow in a separate invoice.

Please confirm once the payment is on its way.
